account I felt like I had to spend it.

I had deprivation spending.

have the money for that,’ your brain
wires itself to believe money will always
run out. So the second you get some,
you spend it before it disappears.

It’s not lack of discipline.
It’s survival mode.

blocks.text:
7 things the gym taught me that have
nothing to do with lifting

My first year taught me:
Motivation might get you started, but
discipline builds the woman you want to
become.

The plateau taught me:
Just because I can’t see progress doesn’t
mean my body isn’t changing.

The injury taught me:
Resting doesn’t make me weak. Ignoring
my body does.

The cut taught me:
I don’t have to shrink myself to feel worthy
or confident.

The bulk taught me:
Food isn’t the enemy.it’s fuel for the body
I’m building.

The mirror taught me:
My body was never the problem. The way I
spoke to myself was.

The woman I became taught me:
Strength was never just about lifting
heavier. It was about becoming a woman
who trusts herself, chooses herself, and
refuses to quit.

decide.
